definitions.gloss: bite; dental occlusion; alignment of upper and lower teeth
definitions.explanation: The way the upper and lower teeth fit together when the mouth is closed. A common dental term.

definitions.gloss: meshing; engagement (of gears or interlocking parts)
definitions.explanation: By extension, the fit or engagement of any two parts that mesh together, such as gear teeth. Also used figuratively for how two parties or arguments line up.

examples.japanese: {噛|か}み{合|あ}わせが{悪|わる}い。
{歯医者|はいしゃ}で{噛|か}み{合|あ}わせを{調|しら}べてもらった。
examples.english: I had the dentist check my bite.

examples.japanese: {噛|か}み{合|あ}わせがずれていると、{頭痛|ずつう}や{肩|かた}こりの{原因|げんいん}になることがある。
examples.english: If your bite is misaligned, it can cause headaches and shoulder stiffness.

examples.japanese: {歯車|はぐるま}の{噛|か}み{合|あ}わせを{確認|かくにん}する。
examples.english: Check the engagement of the gears.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}の{意見|いけん}の{噛|か}み{合|あ}わせが{悪|わる}く、{議論|ぎろん}が{進|すす}まなかった。
examples.english: The two people's opinions didn't mesh well, and the discussion didn't move forward.

examples.japanese: {機械|きかい}の{部品|ぶひん}の{噛|か}み{合|あ}わせを{細|こま}かく{調整|ちょうせい}した。
examples.english: I carefully adjusted how the machine parts mesh together.

notes:
Noun form of {噛|か}み{合|あ}う (to mesh, to bite into each other). The dental sense is the most everyday use; the mechanical sense is common in engineering contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {噛|か}み{合|あ}わせが{悪|わる}い: have a bad bite; not mesh well
- {噛|か}み{合|あ}わせを{治|なお}す: correct one's bite
- {噛|か}み{合|あ}わせを{調整|ちょうせい}する: adjust the alignment / engagement
- {歯車|はぐるま}の{噛|か}み{合|あ}わせ: meshing of gears

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {噛|か}み{合|あ}う: to mesh, to bite together — the verb form
- {歯並|はなら}び: dental alignment — focuses on how teeth are arranged in a row, not how they meet
